newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan air traffic hit by controllers' go-slow.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan air traffic hit by controllers' go-slow.

text.p: Flights in and out of Kenyan airports were delayed by several hours at the weekend when air traffic control staff staged a go-slow, local newspapers reported.

The Sunday Nation said the controllers, who had earlier announced they would start strike action next weekend, were demanding the formation of an autonomous civil aviation authority, independent of government control, and higher pay.

Planes arriving over Nairobi and Mombasa airports were held for long periods before being given clearance to land, and some outgoing flights were delayed by more than three hours, the newspaper reported.
A cruise ship scheduled to leave Mombasa port on Saturday evening was delayed for more than three hours to await the arrival of parties of tourists joining the ship there.
Kenya Airways, which operates flights from Nairobi to European, Asian and African destinations, said the go-slow was having a serious effect on flight schedules.
Airport sources said the Saturday-Sunday go-slow had apparently taken officials by surprise, as it had not been expected to take place until December 13.
